meta.name: Gabriel India Ltd
meta.about: Gabriel India is part of ANAND Group. The Company has established a significant presence across all automotive customer segments, including OEMs, Aftermarket, and exports. Company manufactures over 500 models of ride control products. [1] Its products include shock absorbers, struts, front forks and others.[2]
meta.keyPoints: Business Overview:[1] Gabriel India is the flagship company of the ANAND Group. It started in ride control and now makes shock absorbers, struts, front forks, sunroofs, drivetrain products, NVH and Body-in-White parts, synchroniser rings, aluminium forgings, and automotive fluids and lubricants. Ride control products serve 2W/3W, PVs, CVs and railways. The company has 80+ R&D specialists and 3 technology centres across India and Europe.
pros: Company has been maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 29.4%

Company's working capital requirements have reduced from 29.1 days to 22.3 days
cons: Stock is trading at 15.2 times its book value

growth.text: Latest quarter Q1FY27: revenue +15.5% YoY, profit +2.0% YoY.

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 8.6%–9.6% since FY24 (peak FY25, trough FY24); FY26 was 9.4%.
Q1FY27 operating margin of 8.7% is lower than 38.4% of the 86 quarters on record — mid-range for the company.

returns.text: ROE was 19.8% in FY26 (range 17.9–22.4% since FY24).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 28.3% vs headline ROCE of 26.0% — little distortion from the treasury book.
DuPont FY26: net margin 5.4% × asset turnover 2.1x × leverage 1.7x.

balance.text: Net cash of ₹176 cr (cash + investments less borrowings), 12.9% of net worth.

cash.text: Over 3 years the business generated ₹726 cr of operating cash flow (107.4% of reported profit), spent ₹612 cr on capex and paid ₹176 cr in dividends.
FY26 capex was 2.4x depreciation and 5.1% of sales — an expansion phase.
Cash conversion cycle of 18 days in FY26.

valuation.text: P/E of 71.4x vs since-listing (2.4-year) median 43.3x (range 28.0–73.7x); cheaper than 1.6% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
EV/EBITDA of 43.4x vs since-listing (2.4-year) median 26.0x (range 16.5–44.8x); cheaper than 1.6% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
P/B of 15.2x vs since-listing (2.4-year) median 8.5x (range 4.7–16.6x); cheaper than 4.5% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
At its since-listing (2.4-year) median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹881 vs ₹1,452 today (-39.3%).

price.text: Stock up 13.9% over 1 year; 5y CAGR 56.6%, 10y CAGR 27.5%. Currently 3.1% below its all-time high of ₹1,498.
Versus BSE-500: 13.9% vs -10.5% over 1 year; since 2019, 34.4% vs 11.4% a year.

ownership.text: Foreign institutions raised their stake from 4.1% to 5.9% over 12 quarters.
Promoters raised their stake from 55.0% to 66.3% over 12 quarters.
